name: BricsCAD
meta_desc: BricsCAD offers a familiar DWG interface with powerful 3D modeling, BIM, and mechanical design capabilities.

terms.title: Direct Modeling
terms.definition: Direct Modeling lets users manipulate solid geometry instantly, adding, cutting, or reshaping faces without a parametric history tree, speeding up iterative design.
terms.why_matters: Enables quick concept iterations and reduces file bloat when the design intent changes frequently.
common_pitfalls: Losing design intent when over‑using push‑pull operations
Creating non‑manifold geometry that fails downstream analysis

terms.title: BIM Workflows
terms.definition: BricsCAD includes BIM tools that let users create intelligent building elements (walls, doors, slabs) that carry metadata, supporting clash detection and schedule extraction.
terms.why_matters: Facilitates coordination between architects, MEP engineers, and contractors within a single DWG environment.
common_pitfalls: Missing attribute assignments on BIM objects
Neglecting to update linked 2D plans after 3D changes

terms.title: Mechanical Design Suite
terms.definition: Provides tools for creating sheet metal parts, assemblies, and exploded views directly inside the DWG file, with native BOM generation.
terms.why_matters: Reduces the need for separate mechanical CAD packages, streamlining the product development pipeline.
common_pitfalls: Incorrect layer management for mechanical components
Overlooking tolerance specifications in sheet‑metal folds

terms.title: Parametric Constraints
terms.definition: Constraints such as parallelism, equal length, or concentricity can be attached to entities, ensuring that modifications respect design intent.
terms.why_matters: Guarantees consistency across large assemblies and aids automated updating.
common_pitfalls: Over‑constraining sketches leading to solver failures
Applying constraints to the wrong reference geometry

terms.title: LISP Automation
terms.definition: BricsCAD ships a high‑performance LISP interpreter allowing users to write macros that automate repetitive drawing tasks.
terms.why_matters: Boosts productivity for power users and enables company‑wide standards.
common_pitfalls: Using global variables that persist across sessions
Neglecting error handling causing crashes

terms.title: Dynamic Blocks
terms.definition: Dynamic Blocks embed parameters (scale, rotation, visibility states) allowing a single block definition to represent many variants.
terms.why_matters: Reduces file size and simplifies panel schedule updates.
common_pitfalls: Excessive parameter nesting that becomes hard to maintain
Missing attribute definitions for exported data

terms.title: DWG TrueView Compatibility
terms.short_def: Seamless exchange with Autodesk DWG files.
terms.definition: BricsCAD reads and writes DWG files at the same version levels as Autodesk, ensuring no data loss when collaborating with external firms.
terms.why_matters: Preserves project continuity across mixed‑tool environments.
common_pitfalls: Using unsupported custom objects that dissolve on export
Neglecting to audit line‑type scaling after import

terms.title: Cloud‑Based Collaboration
terms.definition: A hosted service where multiple users can view and edit the same DWG simultaneously, with version control and activity logs.
terms.why_matters: Accelerates design reviews and reduces the need for email attachments.
common_pitfalls: Over‑reliance on internet connectivity
Insufficient permission granularity for external partners

terms.title: Sheet Metal Design
terms.short_def: Specialized tools for bending and unfolding.
terms.definition: Enables creation of flat patterns from 3D sheet metal parts, automatically generating bend tables and material estimates.
terms.why_matters: Speeds up fabrication documentation and reduces manual calculations.
common_pitfalls: Incorrect bend radius settings producing infeasible cuts
Missing K‑factor adjustments for material properties

terms.title: Data‑Driven BIM Attributes
terms.short_def: Linking external data sources to BIM objects.
terms.definition: Allows BIM elements to pull data from spreadsheets or databases (e.g., room schedules, equipment specs) via field mappings.
terms.why_matters: Ensures schedule accuracy and enables automated updates when source data changes.
common_pitfalls: Mismatched column headers causing null values
Over‑loading BIM objects with excessive custom data

terms.title: API Extensibility
terms.short_def: Programmatic access via .NET, C++, and Python.
terms.definition: Developers can create plugins that interact with BricsCAD’s geometry kernel, UI, and data structures, enabling custom toolchains.
terms.why_matters: Tailors the CAD environment to niche industry workflows.
common_pitfalls: Version mismatches between SDK and runtime
Insufficient testing causing crashes in production environments

terms.title: Parametric Assemblies
terms.definition: Components can be nested, with constraints propagating across levels, supporting large mechanical assemblies.
terms.why_matters: Facilitates design reuse and automated BOM extraction.
common_pitfalls: Circular constraints leading to solver divergence
Missing component references after file moves

terms.title: Rendering Module
terms.definition: Provides photorealistic rendering directly from the CAD model, with material libraries and lighting presets.
terms.why_matters: Helps stakeholders visualize design intent without exporting to separate render engines.
common_pitfalls: Excessive polygon count causing long render times
Improper material assignments resulting in unrealistic surfaces

terms.title: Annotation Styles
terms.definition: Customizable annotation templates ensure consistent drawing standards across teams.
terms.why_matters: Reduces re‑drafting effort during QA reviews.
common_pitfalls: Using outdated style sheets that conflict with project standards
Neglecting to update scale factors for large drawings

terms.title: Georeferencing
terms.short_def: Linking CAD geometry to real‑world coordinates.
terms.definition: Sets a coordinate system (e.g., EPSG:4326) for the drawing, enabling integration with GIS data and site plans.
terms.why_matters: Ensures that designs align with survey data and civil infrastructure.
common_pitfalls: Incorrect datum selection causing misalignment
Forgetting to preserve geolocation when exporting to IFC

faqs.question: How do I convert an existing DWG to a BricsCAD BIM model?
faqs.answer: Open the DWG in BricsCAD, run the `BIM2DWG` command, map existing layers to BIM categories, and use the `BIM Import` wizard to generate walls, floors, and structural elements automatically.

faqs.question: Can I use AutoLISP scripts written for AutoCAD in BricsCAD?
faqs.answer: Yes. BricsCAD ships a compatible LISP interpreter; most standard AutoLISP functions work out‑of‑the‑box. Minor API differences (e.g., custom object handling) may require small adjustments.

faqs.question: What is the best workflow for creating sheet‑metal parts?
faqs.answer: Start with a 3D solid, apply the `SheetMetal` command to define thickness, bend radius, and K‑factor, then use `Flatten` to generate the 2D flat pattern for fabrication.

faqs.question: How do I manage version control for large DWG assemblies?
faqs.answer: Enable Bricsys 24/7 cloud storage, check files in/out using the built‑in version manager, and tag releases with meaningful comments. For offline work, integrate with Git‑LFS for binary handling and keep a changelog.

faqs.question: Is there a way to automate dimensioning for repetitive features?
faqs.answer: Create a Dynamic Block with parameters for length/angle, then use the `Block Attribute Manager` to set dimension styles that update automatically when the block is edited.

faqs.question: How can I link external spreadsheets to BIM object attributes?
faqs.answer: Use the `BIM Data Link` tool, select the spreadsheet, map columns to BIM fields (e.g., room number, fire rating), and enable live sync so updates propagate to the drawing instantly.

faqs.question: What are the recommended hardware specs for smooth 3D modeling?
faqs.answer: A quad‑core CPU (Intel i7 or AMD Ryzen 7), 16 GB RAM minimum, a GPU with OpenGL 4.5 support (NVIDIA GTX 1660 or higher), and SSD storage for project files.

faqs.question: Can I export BricsCAD models to IFC for BIM collaboration?
faqs.answer: Yes. Use the `Export IFC` command, choose the appropriate IFC schema (IFC2x3 or IFC4), and configure mapping options for walls, doors, and structural elements before exporting.

faqs.question: How do I create a material library for rendering?
faqs.answer: Open the `Material Editor`, click `New`, define base color, roughness, metallic values, and optionally assign texture maps. Save the library file and reference it in the rendering settings panel.

faqs.question: What is the process for cleaning up a drawing before sending to a client?
faqs.answer: Run `Purge` to remove unused layers and blocks, `Audith` to fix geometry errors, and `Export` to a clean DWG version with the `+audit` flag to ensure compliance with industry standards.

faqs.question: How can I set up custom keyboard shortcuts for frequent commands?
faqs.answer: Open `Options → User Preferences → Keyboard`, click `Customize`, assign your desired key combos to commands, and export the shortcut file for team sharing.

faqs.question: Is there a built‑in clash detection tool?
faqs.answer: BricsCAD includes a lightweight clash detection module under the BIM tab. Select two BIM layers, run `Clash Detect`, and review the generated report highlighting intersecting objects.

faqs.question: How do I generate a BOM from an assembly?
faqs.answer: Select the assembly, run `BOM Generate`, configure attribute fields (part number, quantity, material), and export to CSV or Excel for downstream manufacturing processes.

faqs.question: Can I use Python for automation?
faqs.answer: Yes. BricsCAD provides a Python interpreter (`bricscadpy`). Install the `bricscadpy` package, write scripts using the `pybricscad` API, and run them from the command line or script manager.

faqs.question: What licensing options are available for corporate teams?
faqs.answer: BricsCAD offers network licenses, floating seats, and subscription plans with volume discounts. Contact sales for a customized quote based on user count and feature set.
